T:paper.html:
Superimposing ....

Square, Triangle and Circle 

Constructive Geometry & The Integration of √2 and √3 


The Marusankakushikaku....Is a mysterious Japanese scroll painted by the beloved master artist & monk, Sengai Gibo and is dated to around 1824. It is often referred to as Japan's First Zen Temple. The inscription on the left of the scroll is the name of Sengai's home temple of Shofuku-ji.  In Zen teachings the diagram of these 3 primordial shapes can be interpreted as the underlying building blocks of the "Universe". 

Both, as flat 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional spatial volumes they have historically been used as symbolic and contemplative devices to inspire the mind. The balanced integration of the qualities associated with each symbol is believed to raise one's awareness and  induce realizations of the interconnective order of the cosmos.

The SQUARE is symbolic of the earth and the world of manifestation. The TRIANGLE, as it is in the Pythagorean mystery schools, is symbolic of fire and the world of spirit. The "CIRCLE" is perhaps  in a category of it's own and often referred to as the "ENSO". It is more complex and enigmatic than the others often given contrasting meanings such as 'empty' yet 'full', 'expanding' yet 'limiting', and 'eternal' yet 'cyclical'.

The "LAYING OUT OF THE CIRCLE" is often regarded as the first act of temple building. Keith Critchlow in his book "Time Stands Still", explains that the word 'temple' has its roots in the ancient Greek Temnos, which means "to cut off" or "separate". In Latin.... "templum" meaning "Space", has survived in modern languages as the word 'template', similar to the word "tempus" and confers the adjacent meaning of..."Time" (Critchlow, p22). In the earliest accounts of temple construction, found in the ancient  Hindu manuscript the Manasara Shilpa Shastra, the initial act of temple construction is to establish a central point or axis around which a circle is drawn. This circumscription defines a sacred microcosm within which a transcendent relationship can be established bringing one into attunement with the correct order and harmony of the cosmos. 

With respect to these 3 shapes it is intriguing to consider their combined meaning when aligned to each other and geometrically juxtaposed. Using the circle as the "limiting element" with a radius of  one, or unity, we find that the edge length of the square within the circle is the square root of two (√2), and that the edge length of the triangle within the circle is the square root of three (√3).  It turns out that the edge length of the square, √2,  is precisely the height of a TETRAHEDRON whose base is the same dimensions as the triangle  originally circumscribed within the circle (Fig. 3).

T:excerpt.html: It is intriguing to consider the meaning emerging from the integration of these shapes in terms of both their geometric and mathematical relationships. For if we superimpose the three, using the circle as the limiting shape, we discover a very interesting set of relationships (Fig. 2). Given the radius of the circle as unity or one, we find that the edge length of the square within the circle is the square root of two, and that the edge length of the triangle within the circle is the square root of three. The significance of these relationships is that the edge length of the square is precisely the height of a tetrahedron whose base is the same triangle originally circumscribed by the circle (Fig. 3).

NT:mw9c7x9py6n1.html: In the photo above you can see Bucky's exploration with "parallel ruled lines" of warped planes over the exterior surfaces.  Because of my experience building  kites with internal bracing I decided to do the opposite, to explore the INTERIOR of the Tetra-helix instead. I created the first models using wooden dowels and plastic tubes with colored threads of Red and Blue string crossing through the internal centroids of each tetrahedron from the tetrahedral edges. This created 2 very beautiful hyperbolic-paraboloids that interpenetrated each other, and which in turn created an unexpected "Center Core Channel".  Although the core looks circular when viewed down the axis of the tetrahelix, at any 90º cross section the shape proves to actually be two opposite arcs creating an almond shaped center area similar to the "Vesica Pisces", a very important and meaningful symbol in Christianity and other spiritual belief systems. The Vesica Pisces is a fundamental shape in Sacred Geometry. I began to think that Tetra-Wave was more a model of an eletromagnetic wave or some kind of healing energy form.  This is just one of the many correlations that began to emerge.

NT:mwaocjg9im2k.html:
The first time I saw a Tetrahedron was in a biography entitled "Genius At Work" about Alexander Graham Bell.  Of his many inventions, from the Iron Lung to aircraft wings for the Navy, I loved the large TETRAHEDRON KITES built of metal tubes, some of which were large enough with sufficient force to  lift people and animals right off the ground...defeating gravity!  

Inspired by his tetrahedral kites I started building my own, exploring ways of making them stronger and lighter using internal bracing from opposite outer edges following the natural vectors of edge sub-divisions, what I later learned was called "cell-frequency", and even more recently a mathematical function called "Fractals".

NT:mwb06a6oiyyg.html: I studied "Synergetics" in greater depth in 1984, and became fascinated with his theoretical argument that the traditional X, Y, Z Cartesian coordinate system distorted our understanding of reality. He argued that everything that was alive and existed in Nature, from sub-atomic particals to cosmological structures, whether alive or not, did so based on polyhedral geometry. And that the Tetrahedron was a fundamental form at all scales. He believed that the face-bonded "Tetra-Helix", was a special case, an extension of a single tetrahedron that he believed could explain the structure of DNA. At the time of my reading of Synergetics in 1985, other theories prevailed, but still I felt there might be a connection somehow.
